title: Double `+ - *`: IEEE, NaN from `inf - inf`, `±inf` on overflow
description: `DOUBLE` and `FLOAT` arithmetic is the JVM's, IEEE 754 round to nearest even: `0.1 + 0.2` is 0.30000000000000004. ANSI mode checks no double arithmetic: `inf - inf`, `inf + -inf` and `0 * inf` are NaN, and `1e308 * 10` is +inf, `1e308 + 1e308` +inf, in both modes. `FLOAT` stays single precision (`3e38f * 10f` is +inf as a `FLOAT`, spark-fp32).
Spark's docs state the infinity rules: `inf * 0` is NaN.
reference: `add`, `subtract`, `multiply` round once (`TIE_TO_EVEN`) and raise a domain issue for `inf - inf` and `0 · inf` (`nan_creation`: raise, #257, ST-5); a finite result past the largest double raises (#575, ST-9). Spark is native for rounding and needs guards for the other two.

evidence.note: Floating Point Special Values: positive/negative infinity semantics
`Add`, `Subtract`, `Multiply` on `DoubleType`/`FloatType`: plain Java arithmetic; the exact variants only for integral types

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
